Urra Moor.about: Round Hill on Urra Moor is the highest point of the North York Moors: a trig point on a Bronze Age burial mound, beside the carved Hand Stone guide post.

routes.name: Clay Bank via the Cleveland Way
routes.text: From the Clay Bank car park on the B1257, up the steep climb of Carr Ridge, then east along the broad moorland track.

routes.name: Ingleby Incline
routes.text: From Ingleby Greenhow, up the old Ingleby Incline (a bridleway, the ironstone railway's rope-hauled incline) to Bloworth Crossing, then west along the Cleveland Way. A well-known mountain bike climb.

Cringle Moor.about: A steep-sided moor on the northern escarpment of the Cleveland Hills. The summit is the Drake Howe burial mound; a stone seat and view indicator on Cringle End look out over the Cleveland plain.

routes.name: Lord Stones
routes.text: From the Lord Stones café car park, the Cleveland Way climbs east to the viewpoint on Cringle End; the summit is a short way along the edge.

routes.name: The Three Sisters from Clay Bank
routes.text: West along the Cleveland Way over Hasty Bank and Cold Moor, a switchback of steep drops and climbs along the escarpment.

Stony Ridge.about: A barely-noticeable heather rise on the high watershed above the head of Farndale, scattered with old boundary stones.

routes.name: Old Rosedale railway
routes.text: The trackbed of the old ironstone railway round the head of Farndale, a bridleway and part of the Lyke Wake Walk, passes about a kilometre away; a moor track runs closer.

routes.name: From Blakey Ridge
routes.text: From the Lion Inn at Blakey, follow the railway trackbed west round the head of Farndale. Easy, level going.

Cockayne Ridge.about: The moor at the head of Bransdale, above the hamlet of Cockayne; a broad heather plateau rather than a ridge.

routes.name: Rudland Rigg
routes.text: The old road along Rudland Rigg, between Bransdale and Farndale, passes about a kilometre east. A famous long moorland track for riders, from Gillamoor north to Bloworth Crossing.

routes.name: From the head of Bransdale
routes.text: From the road end near Cockayne, up the moor on shooting tracks.

Ledging Hill.about: A summit at Rosedale Head, crowned by Old Ralph, one of the medieval stone crosses beside the moor road. Its neighbour Young Ralph is the emblem of the National Park.

routes.name: Blakey Ridge road
routes.text: The moor road from Hutton-le-Hole and the Lion Inn to Castleton passes within 300 m; walk across to Old Ralph from Ralph Cross at the road junction.

routes.name: Old Rosedale railway
routes.text: The trackbed of the ironstone railway from Blakey runs round Rosedale Head about a kilometre to the south.

Carlton Bank.about: The western end of the Cleveland Hills escarpment above Carlton-in-Cleveland, with a trig point, a gliding club and a huge view over the Tees plain.

routes.name: Lord Stones
routes.text: From the Lord Stones café car park, a short, steep climb west on the Cleveland Way.

routes.name: Carlton-in-Cleveland
routes.text: Up the steep lane to the top of Carlton Bank, then the Cleveland Way to the trig.

Noon Hill.about: A heather top on Bilsdale West Moor near the Green Howe burial mounds, north of the Bilsdale TV mast.

routes.name: From Chop Gate
routes.text: From Chop Gate in Bilsdale, climb west onto Bilsdale West Moor by the bridleway past Cock Howe, then north along the moor.

routes.name: From Raisdale
routes.text: From the Raisdale road, up the moor tracks from the north.

Cock Heads.about: A broad, featureless heather top on the moor between the heads of Rosedale and Glaisdale.

routes.name: From Rosedale Head
routes.text: From the Knott Road or the Blakey road at Rosedale Head, east across the moor on paths and shooting tracks.

routes.name: George Gap and Cut Road
routes.text: Two moorland bridleways, George Gap and Cut Road, cross the moor about a kilometre from the top.

Cock Howe.about: A Bronze Age burial mound on Bilsdale West Moor, with an old boundary stone beside it.

routes.name: From Chop Gate
routes.text: From Chop Gate in Bilsdale, the bridleway west over Bilsdale West Moor towards Hawnby passes right by the mound.

routes.name: Along the moor from Noon Hill
routes.text: Half a kilometre south of Noon Hill on the moor path.

Black Hambleton.about: The northern end of the Hambleton Hills, crossed by the Hambleton Drove Road, an ancient cattle droving route now followed by the Cleveland Way.

routes.name: Square Corner via the Drove Road
routes.text: From Square Corner above Osmotherley, south along the Cleveland Way on the old Hambleton Street, a byway popular with riders, then a short climb to the trig.

routes.name: From Kepwick or Over Silton
routes.text: Steep bridleways climb the western escarpment from the villages below to join the Drove Road.
